change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor, and the full text and PDF have been replaced by the withdrawal statement. The editor was told that the indoor temperature records analysed in the paper had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and the reported results cannot be relied on. The paper's headline results, including a 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats, came from the indoor temperature data, and another headline result was that living rooms in green-roofed flats spent 41% fewer hours above 28 °C.
evaluation: Your draft sets the indoor cooling effect of a green roof in its model to 2.1 °C, and it describes that value as the reduction in daily peak indoor temperature measured by Okafor et al. [14], while the parameter is described in Section 2.2. The paper reported a mean daily peak indoor temperature 2.1 °C lower in green-roofed flats than in paired control flats. Your draft says its estimate rests above all on the size of the indoor cooling effect, and that the green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C it takes from Okafor et al. [14], while if that value were halved, green roofs would no longer outperform reflective coatings. The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor: the indoor temperature records analysed in it had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. The paper's full text and PDF have been replaced by the withdrawal statement.
recommendation: The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor, and the indoor temperature records analysed in the paper had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. Your draft sets the indoor cooling effect of a green roof in its model to 2.1 °C, and it describes that value as the reduction in daily peak indoor temperature measured by Okafor et al. [14], while the paper reported a mean daily peak indoor temperature 2.1 °C lower in green-roofed flats than in paired control flats. Your draft says the green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C it takes from Okafor et al. [14], and that if that value were halved, green roofs would no longer outperform reflective coatings. Stop and raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, because rewording the text won't fix it. Replace the parameter in Section 2.2 with a value from a reliable source, re-run the model, and then re-check the Discussion's estimate and its comparison with reflective coatings, removing citation [14] from both places.
